chain.label: No regulatory standard for Part 135 operational control, personnel qualification, or single-engine load manifests
chain.trigger: the methods by which operators perform their operational control functions are not defined by regulation

chain.label: Flight followers, coordinators, and operations control specialists untrained and unqualified for operational control duties
chain.trigger: essential operational control functions... were performed without adequate company procedures or by individuals who lacked the training, knowledge, or experience to effectively perform such critical safety duties

caused_by.evidence: the regulations do not specify any training or qualification standards for the personnel who perform these tasks (other than what applies for pilots and certain managers)

chain.label: Company risk assessment, flight release, weather-check, loading, and flight-locating procedures not carried out
chain.trigger: company personnel routinely failed to complete the assessment before flights

caused_by.evidence: their duties are not defined by regulation for Part 135 operations (except for the flight-locating requirement specified in 14 CFR 135.79)

neither of the flight coordinators assigned to the accident flight discussed the flight risks with the accident pilot (as required by company procedures), and neither had received any company training on the risk assessment program

chain.label: Flight-support personnel failed to identify, verify, or relay en route weather and fuel hazards to the pilot
chain.trigger: crucial meteorological risks for the accident flight, including the potential for snow, icing, and reduced visibility along the accident flight route, were not identified before the flight departed

caused_by.evidence: the operations control specialist who handled the accident flight understood some aspects of aviation weather planning but did not fully use the weather tool available for preflight and in-flight planning
the flight scheduler on duty and the accident pilot did not discuss the weather conditions or an agreement about the safety of the flight

chain.label: Routes over mountainous, remote terrain lacking IFR infrastructure
chain.trigger: many passenger, cargo, and mail-carrying operations in Alaska operate in areas of challenging weather and terrain and serve remote areas that lack the... infrastructure needed to support instrument flight rules (IFR) operations

chain.label: Pilots initiated or continued VFR flights into marginal weather, and departed with inadequate fuel, without risk-management support
chain.trigger: most of the described accidents involved pilots' improper decision-making concerning weather-related hazards

caused_by.evidence: the system provided the weather information for an erroneous destination, showing visual meteorological conditions for that location when the weather at the actual destination was IMC. The flight would not have been cleared to depart if the correct weather information had been used
the decision to initiate the accident flight rested solely with the accident pilot, who had less than 2 months' experience flying air tours in southeast Alaska

chain.label: Flights encountered IMC or reduced visibility en route
chain.trigger: an airplane operated as a commuter flight under VFR encountered IMC and crashed into mountainous terrain

caused_by.evidence: the accident flight departed into weather conditions that were below VFR

chain.label: Flights continued at altitudes below surrounding peaks with obscured terrain ahead
chain.trigger: The PIC chose a routing in which the flight encountered an area of deteriorating visibility while at altitudes below the elevation of the adjacent mountain peaks

caused_by.evidence: the pilot made several turns in various locations where the investigation determined the mountain peaks were obscured by clouds
he had flown into a different valley surrounded by much higher terrain and was unsuccessful in his attempt to clear it

chain.label: Aircraft operated below minimum fuel reserve to exhaustion
chain.trigger: the pilot departed knowing that the helicopter did not have the required 20-minute fuel reserve on board

caused_by.evidence: the pilot informed the communication specialist before takeoff that he did not have enough fuel to reach the hospital and requested help locating a nearby fueling location
neither the communication specialist nor the accident pilot contacted a company manager or the operations control center... for guidance about the fuel situation

chain.label: Loss of engine power in flight
chain.trigger: lost engine power due to fuel exhaustion and crashed near Mosby, Missouri

caused_by.evidence: an airplane operated under IFR as an emergency medical services flight lost engine power due to fuel exhaustion

chain.label: Single-engine aircraft loaded over gross weight with CG aft of limit
chain.trigger: the airplane was loaded about 76 lbs over the maximum gross takeoff weight with a center of gravity (CG) aft of the rear limit

caused_by.evidence: Title 14 CFR 135.63(c) requires Part 135 operators of multiengine aircraft to prepare a load manifest for each flight... the FAA has repeatedly declined to take the recommended action

although the company's operations specifications contained aircraft loading procedures that addressed determining weight and balance for its single-engine aircraft, the accident flight was not conducted in compliance with these procedures

chain.label: Aerodynamic stall from degraded performance and insufficient elevator authority
chain.trigger: the airplane's elevator control authority was insufficient to overcome the nose-up pitching moment generated by the loading and the aircraft configuration, and the airplane entered an aerodynamic stall

caused_by.evidence: its out-of-limit weight-and-balance condition increased its stall speed and degraded its climb performance, stability, and slow-flight characteristics

chain.label: Departure from controlled flight after stall
chain.trigger: the airplane slowly lifted off, attained a nose-high attitude, and cleared the trees at the end of the lake before it turned left, rolled left, and crashed

caused_by.evidence: entered an aerodynamic stall and crashed shortly after takeoff from a lake

sustained substantial damage following an in-flight loss of control due to an accumulation of airframe icing... the airplane's loading exceeded the maximum weight limit... for flight in known icing conditions by about 800 lbs

chain.label: Collision with terrain
chain.trigger: the airplane crashed in a manner consistent with controlled flight into terrain

caused_by.evidence: encountered poor visibility conditions and crashed into mountainous terrain
lost engine power due to fuel exhaustion and crashed
it turned left, rolled left, and crashed

chain.label: Fatalities and serious injuries, worsened by delayed search and rescue
chain.trigger: 12 accidents involving Part 135 operators that highlighted operational control or flight-locating deficiencies and resulted in 45 fatalities and 13 serious injuries

caused_by.evidence: The pilot and four passengers sustained fatal injuries
the delayed notification of search and rescue organizations contributed to the severity of the surviving passenger's injuries
